title: Interplay of Chemical Disorder, Vortex Pinning, and Electron Correlations in the Mechanically Robust Medium-Entropy Alloy Superconductor $\text{Nb}_{0.45}\text{Ta}_{0.25}\text{Ti}_{0.15}\text{Hf}_{0.15}$
authors: Pooja Chourasia, Samiul Sk, Nikita Sharma, B. Vignolle, Abhishek Sarkar, Olivier Toulemonde, Sanjoy Mahatha, S. K. Panda, Sourav Marik
abstract: Medium and high-entropy alloys have emerged as a promising class of superconducting materials because their intrinsic chemical disorder can simultaneously enhance mechanical robustness and modify superconducting properties. Here, we present a combined experimental and first-principles investigation of the structural, superconducting, electronic, and local lattice-distortion characteristics of the mechanically robust medium-entropy alloy $\text{Nb}_{0.45}\text{Ta}_{0.25}\text{Ti}_{0.15}\text{Hf}_{0.15}$. The material shows type-II superconductivity with a transition temperature $T_C^{onset} \approx 7.8 ~\mathrm{K}$. A high critical current density of $J_c = 0.48 \times 10^{6}~\mathrm{A/cm^2}$ is observed, and this is attributed to strong vortex pinning at grain boundaries. Specific-heat analysis indicates a strong electron-phonon coupling ($λ$ = 1.07) with a large isotropic s-wave superconducting gap. Density functional theory calculations explicitly model the intrinsic chemical disorder, predict a stable body-centered cubic phase. These calculations further reveal a metallic electronic structure with substantial Ti- and Ta-derived states at the Fermi level. Additionally, our results quantify a pronounced disorder-induced local lattice distortion ($Δd = 0.086$ A), providing a microscopic basis for the experimentally observed enhanced vortex-pinning landscape. Remarkably, the alloy also exhibits an unusually large Kadowaki-Woods ratio, placing it close to the heavy-fermion regime and indicating enhanced electronic correlations beyond conventional alloy superconductors. Our results demonstrate that entropy-engineered chemical disorder can stabilize robust superconductivity, promote strong flux pinning, and induce correlated electronic behavior, establishing refractory medium-entropy alloys as a promising platform for next-generation superconducting materials.
summary: This work presents a comprehensive study of a medium-entropy alloy superconductor, linking its enhanced superconducting performance to its intrinsic chemical disorder. By combining experiments and DFT calculations, the authors demonstrate that disorder stabilizes the superconducting phase, enhances flux pinning, and induces correlated electronic behavior, making these alloys promising for next-generation superconducting applications.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex interplay between intrinsic chemical disorder, vortex pinning mechanisms, and electronic correlations in medium-entropy alloy superconductors.
main_result: The alloy exhibits robust superconductivity ($T_C \approx 7.8$ K) and high critical current density, which is attributed to disorder-induced local lattice distortions that enhance vortex pinning and promote correlated electronic behavior.
method: The research combines experimental characterization (XRD, SQUID, specific heat) with advanced first-principles calculations using the Special Quasirandom Structure (SQS) approach within DFT.
model_or_system: The physical system is the medium-entropy alloy $	ext{Nb}_{0.45}	ext{Ta}_{0.25}	ext{Ti}_{0.15}	ext{Hf}_{0.15}$, which forms a body-centered cubic (bcc) structure and is characterized by significant substitutional chemical disorder.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_C \approx 7.8$ K), high critical current density ($J_c = 0.48 	imes 10^6 	ext{ A/cm}^2$), strong electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda = 1.07$), and a large Kadowaki-Woods ratio.
important_parameters: Disorder-induced local lattice distortion ($\Delta d = 0.086$ Å); superconducting upper critical field ($\mu_0H_{c2}(0) = 7.14$ T).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed enhanced superconducting properties are a direct consequence of the interplay between chemical disorder, lattice distortion, and electronic correlations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural confirmation (XRD, FESEM), the electronic structure (DOS, band dispersion), and the lattice dynamics (phonon dispersion), all modeled using the SQS supercell.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first characterizing the material's structure and basic properties, then using DFT/SQS to model the electronic structure and lattice dynamics, and finally linking the quantified disorder effects ($\Delta d$) to the macroscopic superconducting and transport properties.
why_interesting: The explicit modeling of chemical disorder via SQS to explain enhanced superconducting parameters and correlated behavior provides a powerful, generalizable framework for designing novel superconducting materials.
